draft.title: Causes of urban concentration
card: Australia's big cities are mostly on the coast for historical reasons. British settlement began in 1788 at Sydney Cove, a harbour where ships could land people and supplies.
Each colony later grew around one main port city, such as Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide, Perth and Hobart. The colonial government, banks and businesses were based there.
Farm and mining products, such as wool and wheat, were sent overseas by ship. Roads and railways led to the ports, so jobs and people gathered in those cities.
Much of the inland is dry, with little water for farming and towns. It supports few people, so most of the population stayed near the coast.
draft.remember: Ports, colonial capitals, exports and a dry inland all pulled people to a few coastal cities.

a.q: Why did colonial capitals such as Adelaide and Perth grow much larger than inland towns?
opts: Governments, trade and jobs were based in these port cities
Inland areas were closed to settlers by colonial governments
The coast has always had more farmland than any inland area
Ships could not carry goods to or from the inland towns
a.why: The colonial government, banks and export trade were based in each port city, which drew people to them. Inland areas were not closed to settlers, but the dry climate supported fewer people.
a.clue: Think about where government and trade were based.

b.q: Rosa says Australians live on the coast because the inland is too dry. Which fact about history best adds to her explanation?
opts: Wool and wheat left Australia by ship from port cities
Most Australian rivers run from the coast toward the inland
Settlers in 1788 chose the coast because it had no people
Colonial capitals were built in the centre of each colony
b.why: Exports were shipped from ports, so railways and jobs gathered in coastal cities. This adds a historical reason to the climate reason Rosa gave. Colonial capitals were port cities, not in the centre of each colony.
b.clue: Think about how goods were sent overseas.

a.best: Governments, trade and jobs were based in these port cities

b.best: Wool and wheat left Australia by ship from port cities

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about where government and trade were based' points straight to the only option that mentions government and trade, so it gives the answer away.
The clue 'Think about how goods were sent overseas' matches only one option, the one about wool and wheat leaving by ship, so it gives the answer away.

The distractor 'Settlers in 1788 chose the coast because it had no people' repeats the false terra nullius idea. Aboriginal people lived there, and the why never corrects this, so a student could leave with the myth reinforced.

card: Australia's big cities are mostly on the coast for historical reasons. Aboriginal peoples already lived across the continent when British settlement began in 1788 at Sydney Cove, a harbour on Gadigal land where ships could land people and supplies.
Each colony later grew around one main port city, such as Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide, Perth and Hobart. The colonial government, banks and businesses were based there.
Farm and mining products, such as wool and wheat, were sent overseas by ship. Roads and railways led to the ports, so jobs and people gathered in those cities.
Much of the inland is dry, with little water for farming and towns. It supports few people, so most of the population stayed near the coast.
proposal.remember: Ports, colonial capitals, exports and a dry inland all pulled people to a few coastal cities.

a.q: Why did colonial capitals such as Adelaide and Perth grow much larger than inland towns?
opts: Governments, trade and jobs were based in these port cities
Inland areas were closed to settlers by colonial governments
The coast has always had more farmland than any inland area
The inland was too wet and swampy for building large towns
a.why: The colonial government, banks and export trade were based in each port city, which drew people and jobs there. Inland areas were not closed to settlers. Much of the inland is dry, not wet, so it supports few people.
a.clue: What did a colonial capital have that an inland town did not?

b.q: Rosa says Australians live on the coast because the inland is too dry. Which fact about history best adds to her explanation?
opts: Wool and wheat left Australia by ship from port cities
British settlement began at an inland town in 1788
Colonial capitals were built in the centre of each colony
Railways in each colony were built to lead away from ports
b.why: Exports were shipped from ports, so railways and jobs gathered in coastal cities. This adds a historical reason to the climate reason Rosa gave. Colonial capitals were port cities on the coast, not in the centre of each colony.
b.clue: Rosa gave a reason about climate. Look for one about the past that is true.

problems.detail: 'Farm and mining products, such as wool and wheat' gives only farm products as examples, so students get no mining example. Add one, such as gold, or drop 'and mining'.

Perth is listed as a port city, and question a calls Adelaide and Perth 'port cities'. Perth's main seaport was Fremantle, and Adelaide's was Port Adelaide. Saying they grew around a port and its trade is more accurate.

The remember line says a dry inland 'pulled' people to the coast. The card presents the dry inland as a reason people stayed away from the inland, not as a pull toward the coast, so the line slightly misstates the idea.
